sampling_model.design: A binary randomized instrument \(Z\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(\rho)\), independent of the saturated response type.
sampling_model.units: \(O_i=(Z_i,X_i,Y_i)\), \(i=1,\ldots,n\), are independent and identically distributed draws from \(P\).
sampling_model.treatment: \(X\) takes values in finite \(\mathcal E\); categories in \(T\) share well-defined outcomes across instrument arms and categories in \(U\) impose no cross-arm outcome restriction.
sampling_model.overlap: Only instrument-arm positivity \(0<\rho<1\) is required; exposure cells may have probability zero.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: All observable inputs are finite arm-cell probabilities estimated by empirical conditional frequencies; the finite-sample theorem does not estimate a smooth nuisance function.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: For binary instrument, treatment, and outcome, the sharp average-treatment-effect interval is the maximum and minimum of eight affine response-type expressions.
With binary instrument and outcome and three well-defining exposure levels, the pairwise risk-difference bounds add the third-level terms to the classical binary list.

Under exclusion for every category, inequalities indexed by coordinate subsets characterize the compatible joint counterfactual distributions for arbitrary finite categorical instrument, treatment, and outcome.
For the stated finite response-function class, dual vertex enumeration yields valid and tight symbolic bounds for linear causal queries.
One multinomial Kullback--Leibler confidence region yields simultaneous finite-sample coverage for linear functionals of the fully valid categorical-IV counterfactual law.
Identification gains for binary average-treatment-effect bounds can be decomposed into contributions from instrument information and model features.

body.tldr: A binary randomized instrument and binary outcome are observed with an arbitrarily fine categorical exposure, but exclusion is credible only for a declared subset of categories. The sole identification kernel is a sharp pairwise-effect envelope governed by a two-diagonal capacity: each endpoint is the envelope of the eight Balke--Pearl affine pieces and exactly two pieces for every trusted nuisance category, with finite response laws attaining both endpoints. A perturbation-stable three-category family is selected-trust compatible on an open set yet violates a necessary full-exclusion inequality of Song et al.; a separate open region shows strict improvement over trusting only the two targets. A finite-sample whole-set band is valid at ties and zero cells, and a short Outlook asks for a uniformly valid boundary-spliced Gaussian rectangle with a strict expected-total-width gain on regular compact classes.

project_justification.gap: Published closed forms cover binary treatment and selected small-support coarsenings, while the arbitrary finite categorical-IV characterization imposes exclusion at every treatment level and leaves pairwise effects to generic optimization. The selected-trust regime strictly contains observed laws excluded by that full model, yet can strictly tighten the two-target Balke--Pearl envelope on an open set.
project_justification.niche: Applied adherence studies often have two interventionally meaningful target categories, several scientifically defensible intermediate categories, and residual categories for which no cross-arm exclusion statement is credible.
project_justification.fill: The two-diagonal transport reduction gives the sharp linear-size envelope and finite attaining response laws for this mixed-validity regime; trust updates, wholly untrusted refinements, and one-pass evaluation follow as consequences of the same formula.

body.related_work: Balke and Pearl derive the eight sharp affine ATE pieces for binary instrument, treatment, and outcome by response-function linear programming. Gabriel, Sachs, and Sjolander distinguish well-defining from ill-defining coarsened exposure levels, obtain the ternary boundary formulas, and identify arbitrary exposure cardinality as ongoing work. Sachs, Jonzon, Sjolander, and Gabriel provide the symbolic primal--dual machinery that informs certification of every displayed face with a feasible response law. Song, Guo, Chan, and Richardson use finite-set Strassen theory to characterize arbitrary categorical IV models when exclusion holds at every treatment category. Their coupling construction informs the proof, but every law in the explicit perturbation-stable family \(p^{\rm sep}\) is selected-trust compatible throughout a positive-cell neighborhood and violates their necessary full-exclusion compatibility inequality; separately, the full-trust-compatible table \(p^{\rm gain}\) shows that trusting an intermediate category strictly tightens the two-target envelope on an open neighborhood. Bhadane, Mooij, Boeken, and Zoeter establish the observed full-exclusion compatibility boundary for binary instrument and outcome. VanderWeele and Hernan clarify why coarse treatment labels may conceal distinct versions, and Marshall shows that coarsening can distort conventional IV estimands; these papers provide context for the formula remark on wholly untrusted refinement. Zhang, Frazier, Poskitt, and Zhao analyze identification gains for binary ATE bounds; the categorywise active-face update is only a corollary of the sharp envelope. Du Toit and collaborators supply the LEAP experiment in which the sharp envelope determines whether separately justified intermediate consumption categories change the low-versus-high interval.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The phrase \(8+2|T\setminus\{a,b\}|\) denotes a complete affine evaluation list for each endpoint, not an assertion that every listed term is an irredundant facet on every lower-dimensional support stratum. Formula remark: a wholly untrusted refinement obeys \(L_{\widetilde T}(\widetilde p)=L_T(p)\) and \(U_{\widetilde T}(\widetilde p)=U_T(p)\); push a factual coupling forward through \(g\), and lift it by arbitrary disintegration within each untrusted fiber. Implementation note: compute the eight baseline faces, scan \(c\in T\setminus\{a,b\}\), update the lower maximum and upper minimum with the two category faces, and retain ties; this uses \(O(|\mathcal E|)\) arithmetic and \(O(1)\) auxiliary memory beyond the input and active-face output. These are formula and implementation consequences, not independent research targets. Producing a full attaining transport by generic augmenting paths is claimed only to terminate in finite polynomial time.
body.honest_scope: The sole identification kernel is the sharp-envelope theorem with its transport completion and finite endpoint-attaining laws. The perturbation-stable non-representability family and the separate open strict-gain region provide the load-bearing comparison with the full-exclusion model of Song et al.; the Hoeffding whole-set theorem supplies finite-sample coverage. The categorywise trust update is a one-line corollary, wholly untrusted refinement is a formula remark, and one-pass evaluation is an implementation note. The bounded computations are diagnostic evidence: the supplied checker reported agreement across \(840\) response-law linear programs, \(9{,}648\) exact rational endpoint constructions, and the exact LEAP interval \([-5073/31720,10/61]\); the denominator-three early-kill enumeration reported \(109{,}440\) exact endpoint constructions. These checks are not theorem premises. The Outlook question remains open over triangular arrays without cell, face-gap, or face-variance floors, while its strict precision comparison is restricted to nonempty compact regular classes. No monotonicity, exposure ordering, instrument relevance, exposure-cell positivity, or clinical justification of any trusted LEAP category is claimed.
